# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 32 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 32 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_032_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 4, Chapter 2 — Post-Baptismal Repentance

**1** I asked him again: "Sir, I have heard from certain teachers that there is no other repentance than the one we received at baptism — when we went down into the water and received forgiveness of our former sins." **2** He replied, "You have heard correctly, for that is indeed so. For one who has received forgiveness of sins should sin no more but should dwell in purity. **3** However, since you inquire diligently into all things, I will show you this also — not to provide a pretext for error to those about to believe or who have recently believed in the Lord. For those who have recently believed or are about to believe have no repentance for sins but only a remission of their former sins. **4** But for those who received the call in the earlier days — for them the Lord established repentance. For the Lord, who knows the heart and foreknows all things, knew the weakness of human beings and the many devices of the devil — that he would do some harm to the servants of God and deal wickedly with them. **5** Therefore in his great mercy the Lord had compassion on his creation and established this repentance, and the authority over this repentance was given to me. **6** But I tell you this: if after this great and holy calling anyone is tempted by the devil and sins, he has one repentance available. But if he sins and repents again and again, it profits such a person nothing — for he will with difficulty live to God." **7** I said, "I have come alive in hearing you so carefully explain this — for I know that if I add no more sins I shall be saved." He replied, "You shall be saved — you and all who do these things."

---

*LOGOS note: The theological position here is carefully nuanced: baptism provides full forgiveness of pre-Christian sin. Post-baptismal sin can be forgiven ONCE through this special divine provision. But habitual sinning-and-repenting renders the repentance worthless. This is the Shepherd's middle position between "no post-baptismal repentance" (Hebrews 6) and "unlimited repentance."*
